copy.heroHeading: The renovations that need an engineer
copy.storyHeading: We started by fixing other people's extensions
story: Setia Craft was founded in 2015, and a surprising share of our early work was repairing extensions built by contractors who had never sized a footing. Cracked slabs, sagging beams, additions that could never be approved or refinanced.

Eleven years on, structural work is all we do. Every job goes through a registered engineer and every plan gets submitted — which makes us slower and dearer than the alternative, and is exactly the point.

process.title: Assess the Structure
process.text: Before pricing anything we look at what is actually holding your house up. Footing size, beam spans, soil conditions. Sometimes the answer is that what you want is not possible as drawn — better to hear that now.

process.title: Engineer & Submit
process.text: A registered engineer designs and endorses the structural work, and we lodge the submission with the council. Approval takes three to five months and we will not start structural work without it.

process.title: Build to Drawing
process.text: Built exactly to the endorsed drawings, with the engineer inspecting at footing and beam stages. You receive as-built drawings and the approval documents at handover.
